Work in worktree /opt/nxeon-wt-track (branch feature/ads-tracking). Do NOT deploy, do NOT run prisma commands. Verify types with `npx tsc --noEmit` (node_modules is symlinked; if missing run `ln -s /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules` but NEVER `prisma generate`). Commit on the branch when done; report files changed.

GOAL: fire real conversion events on the order/signup funnels using the tracking layer already built on this branch. The pieces that exist: lib/tracking.ts exports `sendMetaConversion({eventName,eventId?,email?,value?,currency?,sourceUrl?})` (server-side Meta CAPI, returns {ok,eventId}); components/marketing/ConversionTags.tsx installs a browser global `window.nxTrack(evt, {value,currency,eventId})` that fires Meta Pixel + Google Ads/GA4.

DO NOT TOUCH lib/actions-hosting.ts or anything under app/dashboard/hosting or worker/hosting.ts (another agent owns the hosting branch). Only the VPS-order + signup funnels here.

1. VPS order "Purchase": read lib/actions.ts `payAndDeploy` (~line 422) and lib/order.ts `placeOrder` (~389). Find where an order SUCCEEDS (server-side). There, after success, call `sendMetaConversion({eventName:'Purchase', email:user.email, value: <charged dollars>, currency:'USD'})` (best-effort, never throw into the order path — wrap in try/catch), and return the resulting `eventId` to the client in the action's result. Then in the client that calls it (components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx and/or app/dashboard/deploy) fire `window.nxTrack('Purchase',{value,currency:'USD',eventId})` on success (guard `typeof window.nxTrack==='function'`).
2. Signup "Lead": lib/actions.ts `register` (~145) — on successful account creation call `sendMetaConversion({eventName:'Lead', email})` server-side. Fire `window.nxTrack('Lead')` on the client signup-success path.
3. Create components/marketing/FireConversion.tsx — a tiny "use client" component that takes {event,value?,currency?,eventId?} and calls window.nxTrack on mount via useEffect (for success pages that render server-side). Use it where a redirect/render (not a client handler) is the success signal.

Keep it best-effort everywhere (a tracking failure must never break an order or signup). Match existing code style. tsc clean, commit.

content.text:
Done. Committed to `feature/ads-tracking` as `a019565`. `npx tsc --noEmit` passes clean. No deploy, no prisma commands run. Did not touch `lib/actions-hosting.ts`, `app/dashboard/hosting`, or `worker/hosting.ts`.

## What I did

Both order-success paths and the signup path complete via a **server-side redirect**, so there is no client submit handler that observes success in place. The correct realization of the tracking spec is therefore: fire the server-side Meta CAPI event at the success point, carry its `eventId` (and charged dollars) on the redirect, and fire the browser pixel on the destination page via the new `FireConversion` component. The shared `eventId` dedupes CAPI + pixel to one conversion.

**Files changed:**
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-track/components/marketing/FireConversion.tsx` (new) — tiny `"use client"` component; calls `window.nxTrack(event,{value,currency,eventId})` once on mount, guarded on `typeof ... === "function"`, wrapped in try/catch.
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-track/lib/actions.ts`:
  - `register` (~145): fires `sendMetaConversion({eventName:'Lead', email})` after account creation; redirects to `/dashboard?lead=1&ev=<id>`.
  - `payAndDeploy` (~422): after `placeOrder` succeeds on the wallet/free branch, fires `Purchase` with `quote.chargeCents/100` (skipped for free admin grants); redirects to `/dashboard/servers/<id>?purchased=1&val=<dollars>&ev=<id>`.
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-track/lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` — card-paid order branch: after `placeOrder`, fires `Purchase` with `order.sold.chargeCents/100`. `claim()` guarantees exactly one fulfilling caller, so CAPI fires once even across the confirm-route/webhook race; the `eventId` rides the redirect.
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-track/app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` — reads `purchased/val/ev` params, renders `<FireConversion event="Purchase" ...>`.
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-track/app/dashboard/page.tsx` — added `searchParams`, renders `<FireConversion event="Lead" eventId={ev}>` on `lead=1`.
- `.gitignore` — added `node_modules` (the symlink kept getting picked up by `git add`); the symlink is not committed.

## Notes for the caller
- All conversion calls are best-effort (try/catch, `console.error` on failure) and never throw into the order/signup path.
- `DeployWizard.tsx` was intentionally **not** modified: its wallet-success path redirects server-side (never returns a client result) and its card path navigates to Stripe, so it has no client-observable success moment — the redirect-landing `FireConversion` is the correct client fire point, which is exactly the use case point 3 describes.
- Dedup relies on `eventId`, so even a page refresh with the params still present re-fires the same id and Meta collapses it to one conversion (GA4 could double-count a manual refresh, a minor edge case).
